title: A living sacrifice (Romans 12:1–2)
hookLine: offer your bodies; be transformed by the renewing of your mind

lines: ELEVEN CHAPTERS OF WHAT GOD HAS DONE.
cards: Sacrifice. The word can bring up something dead: an animal on an altar, smoke going up. Or something given up: the sacrifice fly in baseball, the parent who works two jobs.
Something lost so something else can happen. Now put together two words that don't seem to belong: a living sacrifice.

For eleven chapters, Paul has talked about what God has done: grace, faith, the Spirit, super-conquering. Now he turns a corner. A small word in his first sentence ties what God has done to how to live.
Then he asks for something strange.

teach.b: Here it is, in the King James Bible: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service."
Start with therefore. Everything Paul asks from here grows out of the mercies of God he's already described. Not do this so God will love you, but God has loved you, therefore.
Not just your soul, not just your Sunday: your hands, your feet, your tired back, your Tuesday afternoon.
And a living sacrifice: not killed on an altar, but offered and still breathing, going on with ordinary life as a gift.
The King James says reasonable service; the Greek can mean the worship that makes sense, or spiritual worship. Translators still argue about it.

Then verse two: "And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind." Conformed: pressed into a shape, like dough in a mold. Transformed is a different kind of change.
The Greek is metamorphousthe; you can hear metamorphosis in it, a caterpillar becoming a butterfly. It's the same word the Gospels use for Jesus on the mountain, when he was transfigured and shone.
And it's passive: be transformed. Christians hear that as something God does, not something a person pulls off by effort.

teach.h: BE YE TRANSFORMED BY THE RENEWING OF YOUR MIND.
teach.b: The change starts in the renewing of your mind, in what a person thinks about and dwells on. These two verses open the practical chapters that follow: worship that walks out of church on two feet.

how: Some Christians begin the day by offering it to God, and some traditions, such as the Catholic Morning Offering, have set prayers for this; Romans 12:1–2 is often memorized.

o: giving up something you love to earn God's favor
an animal offered on an altar in the Temple
an ordinary life, body and all, offered to God

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.
p: because of the mercies of God
pressed into a shape, like dough

s: a living sacrifice means something killed on an altar
it's a life offered and still breathing: body, ordinary days and all.
Paul's word for transformed is the same one used for Jesus's transfiguration
Paul asks for this so that God will start loving us
it begins with therefore: because of the mercies of God already given.

games.q: you're Paul. you've spent eleven chapters on what God has done. how do you begin telling people how to live?
o: with a list of rules to earn God's favor.
therefore, by God's mercies, offer your bodies as a living sacrifice.
by telling them to leave the world behind.
games.why: "I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice." the ethics grow out of the grace.

practice: Picture the rest of your day, hour by hour: the commute, the meetings, the dishes, the kids, the errands, nothing special.

Hold it all out in open hands as a gift, not a performance, and feel your feet on the floor and your hands, part of the offering too. If you pray, you can offer the day to God in your own words, or in silence.

wordCard.voice: Living sacrifice. Not something killed on an altar, but a whole ordinary life, body and all, offered to God as a gift.

orig.note: Greek: be transformed. the root of metamorphosis, and the word for Jesus's transfiguration.

carryVoice: Your line: be transformed. Not pressed into a mold, but made new. Day three hundred twenty-six.
